title: Interface Composition
concept: Types can implement many interfaces simultaneously — composing capabilities like Eq + Display + Clone without any hierarchy.
why: Interface composition gives you the power of multiple inheritance without the complexity. A type can be Eq AND Display AND Clone — independent capabilities.
tips: Compose interfaces freely — there's no limit to how many a type can implement
Think of interfaces as 'tags' describing what a type CAN DO
Interface composition is the XIOM way to achieve polymorphism without inheritance
A type's capabilities are the sum of ALL interfaces it implements
common_mistakes: Trying to create interface hierarchies — composition is preferred
Forgetting to implement ALL methods of an interface
Implementing conflicting semantics across interfaces (e.g., Eq says equal, Ord says different)
